description: Master Pillar-Vector Weight Table. 22 pillars × 11 vectors. 1.0 = Critical/Mandatory, 0.5 = Supporting/Useful, 0.0 = Irrelevant (skip to reduce noise).

legend.1.0: Mandatory — Newton must find high-quality data for this cell
legend.0.7: Important — Newton should populate this cell
legend.0.2: Weak — Newton includes only if data is readily available
legend.0.0: Irrelevant — Newton skips this cell entirely

P01_Strategy.label: Strategy
P01_Strategy.note: Strategy is human judgement. Agent can research but cannot decide. Cost and research are the most critical vectors — no plan survives without a budget and evidence.

P02_Experience.label: Experience
P02_Experience.note: Design is skills-led. Tips are critical — bad UX kills retention. Agent can generate wireframes and copy but cannot replace a UX designer's empathy for the user.

P03_Code.label: Code
P03_Code.note: Highest agent autonomy outside Pattern. Agent can generate, review and refactor code near-autonomously. Tech and integration are both critical — wrong stack or poor API design compounds debt.

P04_Database.label: Database
P04_Database.note: Risk is maximum — a corrupt or poorly designed database cannot be easily fixed post-launch. Agent can write schemas and queries but data governance requires human sign-off.

P05_Content.label: Content
P05_Content.note: Content is where agent adds most user-visible value. Prompts are the primary vector — AI generates content from structured inputs. Time is high because content volume is always underestimated.

P06_Hardware.label: Hardware
P06_Hardware.note: Tech and cost are both critical — cloud provider choice and tier lock-in are long-term cost decisions. Agent can generate IaC templates but cannot provision or approve spend.

P07_Pattern.label: Pattern
P07_Pattern.note: This is the agent pillar. Agent weight is 1.0 — AI/LLM/automation patterns ARE agents. Tools and prompts are the two mandatory vectors. Cost is low because patterns replace human labour.

P08_Testing.label: Testing
P08_Testing.note: Risk is maximum — untested code in production causes incidents. Time is critical — testing is always squeezed at end of sprints. Agent can write and run tests near-autonomously.

P09_Deployment.label: Deployment
P09_Deployment.note: Tools and integration are mandatory — CI/CD pipeline is worthless without the integrations (GitHub, registry, cloud). Agent generates pipeline config; human approves production deployments.

P10_Security.label: Security
P10_Security.note: Three 1.0 vectors — tech, research, risk. Security is non-negotiable across all project sizes. Agent can audit code for vulnerabilities but humans must verify findings and sign off pen-test reports.

P11_Actors.label: Actors
P11_Actors.note: Skills and cost are both 1.0 — people are the largest budget item and skills gaps are the most common project killer. Tech weight is 0.1 — people are not a technology choice.

P12_Support.label: Support
P12_Support.note: Tips are mandatory — every support organisation has hard-won lessons. Agent handles L1 triage, monitoring alerts, and incident routing with high autonomy.

P13_Compliance.label: Compliance
P13_Compliance.note: Research and risk are both 1.0. Agent weight is 0.2 — legal requires human sign-off. GDPR fine is 4% of global turnover; no agent can carry that liability.

P14_Scaling.label: Scaling
P14_Scaling.note: Tech and risk are both 1.0 — wrong scaling strategy causes system collapse at the worst moment (launch day). Agent can configure auto-scaling rules but capacity planning needs business context.

P15_Maintenance.label: Maintenance
P15_Maintenance.note: Time is the critical vector for maintenance — tech debt compounds daily. Agent can identify tech debt, suggest dependency upgrades and auto-patch known CVEs.

P16_Sales.label: Sales
P16_Sales.note: Cost and tips are both 1.0 — sales is about economics and hard-won wisdom. Agent can draft proposals and analyse pipeline data but cannot build relationships or close deals.

P17_Marketing.label: Marketing
P17_Marketing.note: Prompts are mandatory — AI generates ad copy, social posts, SEO content and email campaigns. Agent weight is high because content generation is a core agent capability.

P18_Documentation.label: Documentation
P18_Documentation.note: Tools and prompts are both 1.0. Agent can auto-generate API docs, runbooks and user guides from code and schema. Time is 0.9 — documentation is always the last thing and always underestimated.

P19_Integration.label: Integration
P19_Integration.note: Risk and integration are both 1.0 — broken integrations are the #1 cause of production incidents. Three near-1.0 vectors (tech, skills, time) reflect real-world integration pain. Legacy connectors take 2-3x longer than estimated every time.

P20_Architecture.label: Architecture
P20_Architecture.note: Four 1.0 or near-1.0 vectors — skills, research, tips, risk. Wrong architecture is the single most expensive mistake in software. Agent weight is 0.3 — agent suggests patterns, humans decide. ADRs must be human-approved.

P21_ChangeManagement.label: Change Management
P21_ChangeManagement.note: Four 1.0 vectors — skills, time, tips, risk. 70% of digital transformations fail due to change management, not technical failure. Time cannot be compressed — culture moves slowly. Agent weight is 0.2 — agent drafts communications but cannot lead human change.

P22_FinancialGovernance.label: Financial Governance
P22_FinancialGovernance.note: Cost and risk are both 1.0 — running out of money at 80% complete is a leading cause of project failure. Agent models cost scenarios and tracks burn rate; humans make financial decisions and approve spend.

P23_Observability.label: Observability
P23_Observability.note: Observability is infrastructure table stakes at 1k-10k scale and up. Weight heavy on tools + risk + cost (the big procurement decisions); lighter on prompts + agents (those are enabling, not deciding).

switchboard_triggers.P13_Compliance: industry IN [education, finance, health, legal] OR scale > 5000
switchboard_triggers.P14_Scaling: scale > 5000 OR growth_projection == high OR budget_tier >= L3
switchboard_triggers.P21_ChangeManagement: project_status == existing OR team_size > 10 OR budget > 50000
switchboard_triggers.P22_FinancialGovernance: budget > 10000 OR project_duration_months > 3 OR budget_tier >= L2
